# Volume 3 — Chapter VII Home Again

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Those initial three weeks at Wexcombe had appeared lengthy; nevertheless, the remainder of the term sped past on the wings of the wind. Prior to their realizing it, the Wexcombe students found themselves engulfed in the labor of Christmas examinations, coming out of them with varying degrees of triumph. The distinction of topping the Freshman classes shifted among Nell, Hugh and Cressida; Honora performed exceedingly well; Wilfred Mott managed a respectable pass, and conducted himself with as much self-satisfaction as though he were first in every subject.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0000 }

“I am unable to fully accept that by this hour tomorrow Grey Shutters will be my location,” Nell stated as the final evening prior to leaving arrived. “Yet that is where I will be. Meanwhile, Cressy, your destination will be Harborough alongside Hector and Orlando.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0001 }

“I am eager to view them,” confessed Cressy, in the middle of eating her piece of chocolate. “It’s true that they are exceptionally sweet boys, you know. An abundance of dances, drives, and overall festivities is planned. For failing to return home alongside me during the break, Queen Nell, you will never have my forgiveness.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0002 }

“‘Never’ equals three days when it comes to you, Cressy. Asking me was sweet of you—and I’d be thrilled to visit Harborough eventually. However, I am unable to attend this year—returning home is a necessity for me. You cannot fathom the degree to which my heart yearns for it.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0003 }

“Your experience will not be very enjoyable,” Cressy remarked with contempt. “I imagine a couple of quilting bees will take place; additionally, every old busybody will discuss you, both directly and in your absence. My dear, boredom will be the death of you.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0004 }

“In Brierley?” asked Nell, thoroughly entertained.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0005 }

“Now, a completely magnificent time would be yours if you would accompany me. Harborough would be crazy about you, Queen Nell—the way you look, your hair, and, well, all of it! So distinct are you. A huge hit is what you would be—with me soaking up the borrowed fame—‘near the rose, though not the rose itself.’ Please reconsider and come, Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0006 }

“Cressy, your depiction of social successes is very intriguing, but I will create a contrasting image. My destination is a former green, currently somewhat weathered rural farmhouse surrounded by apple trees without leaves. Further down lies a stream, and past that is a fir forest in December where I have listened to rain and wind play upon harps. A neighboring pond will currently appear gray and melancholic. Inside the home, two elderly women will be present, with one being lean and tall, while the other is stout and short; additionally, two twins will be there, with one serving as an ideal example, whereas the other is referred to by Mrs. Sowerby as a ‘holy terror.’ An upper small chamber above the veranda will exist, dense with old memories, alongside a large, plump, wonderful feather mattress that will feel like ultimate comfort following a boardinghouse bed. Cressy, what is your opinion of my image?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0007 }

“It appears to be a rather dreary piece,” Cressy remarked, pulling a face.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0008 }

“Oh, but I omitted the element that changes everything,” Nell uttered gently. “Love will exist there, Cressy—devoted, gentle affection, the kind I will not ever discover anywhere else in the universe—affection that is holding out for me. That turns my painting into a work of art, does it not, even though the hues are somewhat lacking in brightness?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0009 }

Without a word, Cressy stood up, threw her chocolate box aside, approached Nell, and embraced her.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0010 }

“Nell, I desire to be such as you are,” she remarked with gravity.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0011 }

Isolde came to the Delford station to meet Nell on the following evening, and the pair traveled back to their house beneath quiet skies filled with stars. Grey Shutters seemed extremely celebratory while they made their way up the lane. Illumination shone from all the windows, the brightness bursting forth into the night like fire-red flowers hanging before the black backdrop of the Whispering Wood. Furthermore, a bold bonfire burned in the yard, accompanied by two joyful small figures leaping about it, one of whom uttered a bloodcurdling scream when the buggy pulled in beneath the poplar trees.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0012 }

“Robin intends that to be an Indian war-whoop,” Isolde stated. “The hired boy of Mr. Pettifer instructed him in it, and he has been refining it to greet you. Mrs. Sowerby claims her nerves have been worn to a frazzle by it. You see, he sneaks behind her, and then releases it. Furthermore, he was set on having a bonfire to celebrate your arrival. For two weeks he has been stacking branches and harassing Thirza to allow him to douse it with kerosene oil prior to lighting it. Judging by the odor, I believe she permitted it, even though Mrs. Sowerby maintained until the end that Robin would destroy himself and all the others if he were allowed.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0013 }

By this time, Nell had stepped down from the buggy, and Robin was enthusiastically throwing his arms around her knees, while even Lucy held fast to her hand.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0014 }

“Is that not a splendid bonfire, Nell? Allow me to demonstrate how to prod it—do you see those sparks? I made it for your benefit, Nell, because your return home made me so happy.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0015 }

Thirza’s lean figure appeared in the open kitchen doorway, silhouetted against the light inside. Because she feared greatly that joy would make her weep—she, a rigid, restrained Thirza, who considered any showing of intense feeling improper—she chose to encounter Nell in the dimness. Standing behind her was Mrs. Sowerby, cheerful, gentle, and motherly, just as she used to be. The affection that Nell had assured Cressy was anticipating her encompassed her and wrapped her in its grace and gentleness. Indeed, no new thing could equal former bonds, former companions, and former Grey Shutters! Sitting at the well-filled supper table, Nell had such shining eyes, such rosy cheeks, such silvery, bright laughter! Moreover, Isolde intended to spend the entire night there as well. It mirrored the cherished past so closely! Furthermore, the table was adorned with the rose-bud tea-set! For Thirza, this was the absolute limit of her natural capacity.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0016 }

“I expect that you and Isolde will go on chatting until morning,” Thirza uttered mockingly while the girls headed up the stairs. Thirza invariably spoke with sarcasm whenever she exposed her true feelings.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0017 }

“Indeed,” Nell assented cheerfully, “though putting Robin to sleep comes first for me. That is his firm demand.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0018 }

“You bet,” Robin said, while they proceeded down the corridor. “I wish for someone to hear my prayers once more. Saying them by myself is no fun.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0019 }

“You do not speak those words by yourself, Robin. God remains alongside you continuously to listen to you.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0020 }

“Indeed, I am unable to perceive Him,” Robin argued. “My desire is to offer prayers to a person visible to me, yet I refuse to recite them to Thirza or Mrs. Sowerby, so there!”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0021 }

All the same, as soon as Robin was dressed in his gray flannel nighty, starting did not appear to be his top priority. Shifting one unclad foot against the other, he remained in front of Nell with a hesitant expression.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0022 }

“Come along, my sweet, drop to your knees,” Nell requested.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0023 }

Robin approached and pressed his head against the lap of Nell, though he refrained from kneeling.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0024 }

“Nell,” he uttered, his words suppressed. “I do not want to pray anymore. It has been a week since I last felt like doing so. I—I failed to pray yesterday evening as well as the evening prior.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0025 }

“Why wouldn’t you, Robin?” Nell inquired softly.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0026 }

“If I reveal it to you, you won't get angry, will you?” Robin pleaded.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0027 }

Nell picked up the small figure clad in gray flannel onto her knee, nestling his head against her arm.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0028 }

“Is it ever my reaction to become ‘mad’ upon hearing what you have to say, Robin?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0029 }

“Na-a-ay, it never happens with you. Yet you become apologetic, and that is more unpleasant. It will make you terribly sorry when I share this with you, Nell—and I imagine you will feel ashamed on my account.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0030 }

“Did you do a bad thing, Robin, and does that prevent you from saying your prayers?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0031 }

“No, up to this point I have not behaved badly. Nevertheless, committing a misdeed is my desire.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0032 }

“What’s the matter, Robin?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0033 }

“Nell, I—I feel the need to utter a profane word,” Robin uttered abruptly, straining himself to speak. “A week ago, I caught Mr. Pettifer’s hired boy using it, and from that moment on, the urge to speak it has possessed me constantly—including the moments I recite my prayers.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0034 }

“Speak the words then, Robin.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0035 }

In astonishment, Robin raised his reddened face.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0036 }

“However, Nell, the word is terribly bad.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0037 }

“Speak the words!”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0038 }

Robin offered her a second disbelieving glance, after which he uttered the terrible word in a quiet tone. Within moments, he was burying his face into her.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0039 }

“Oh, Nell, I won't ever repeat it—not ever. I won't ever desire to repeat it. That it was bad I was aware, but I didn't think it was this—this—I didn't think it was of that nature.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0040 }

“No, I doubt you will ever wish to utter those words again, Robin—or even ponder them. Also, if I were in your place, I would not associate frequently with the boy hired by Mr. Pettifer.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0041 }

“He is capable of producing splendid battle-cries,” Robin remarked with a slight tinge of regret.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0042 }

“However, you would prefer not to have your mind crammed with vile language, wouldn't you, Robin—terms that are going to corrupt it and expel everything that is virtuous and noble?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0043 }

“No,” Robin stated, staring with the wide-eyed intensity of an owl while lost in thought.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0044 }

“In that case, refrain from accompanying the individuals who employ them. Now, do you believe you are capable of offering your prayers, Robin?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0045 }

“Oh, yes,” said Robin, eagerly squirming lower on his knees, “I am able to say them fine now. I am not afraid now to say ‘if I should die before I wake,’ the way I was when I was wishing to say that word.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0046 }

Likely Nell and Isolde opened up their hearts completely to one another during that night, yet not a single trace of those shared secrets remains. At the morning meal, the pair appeared as luminous and clear-eyed as merely young people are able to look following illicit hours spent feasting and confiding. Prior to this moment, snow had not fallen, yet when Isolde went over the ancient log bridge heading toward home, light white flakes commenced drifting down upon the fields and forests, which lay russet and gray within their deep slumber. Before long, the distant hillsides and high places grew faint and ghost-like behind their thin wrapping, resembling a pale autumn that had tossed a hazy wedding veil across her tresses while awaiting her winter groom. Thus, they enjoyed a white Christmas when all was said and done, and it proved to be a most agreeable day. During the morning hours, correspondence and presents arrived from Miss Rosalind and Cedric; Nell unsealed them inside the inviting Grey Shutters kitchen, an area brimming with what Robin, inhaling with delight, termed “pretty smells.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0047 }

“Miss Rosalind and Mr. Stanhope have taken up residence in their new home now,” Nell reported. “I feel certain Miss Rosalind is completely happy—I can tell from the overall impression of her letter—yet there is a line from Belinda the Fourth. She dislikes Boston immensely, and she is terribly homesick. Miss Rosalind wishes for me to travel to Echo Cottage on some day during my stay at home to burn a fire for ventilation, as well as ensure the cushions are not becoming moldy. I believe I will have Isolde accompany me next week, so we may pass the evening alongside Theodora Dix. I desire to visit Theodora. Incidentally, is Ludovic Speed continuing to visit her?”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0048 }

“That is what people claim,” Thirza remarked, “and it is probable he will keep doing so. Everyone has stopped anticipating that this wooing will ever lead to anything.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0049 }

“If I were Theodora, I would make him move faster,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked. And she unquestionably would have done so.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0050 }

A typical scribble from Cressida arrived as well, packed with Hector and Orlando, the things they stated, the actions they performed, and the expressions on their faces upon catching sight of her.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0051 }

Cressy penned, “However, deciding which one to wed is something I am unable to do yet. My wish is that you had accompanied me so you could choose on my behalf. A decision will need to be made by somebody. My heart pounded heavily upon seeing Hector, making me think, ‘The right man could be him.’ Then, Orlando arrived, causing my heart to pound once more. That offers no direction, even if it ought to based on every novel I have read in my life. Nell, wouldn’t your heart refrain from pounding for anyone other than the true Prince Charming? A fundamental flaw must exist within my own heart. Nevertheless, my time here is absolutely wonderful. I desire so much for you to be present! Snow is falling on this day, bringing me sheer delight. Having a green Christmas was a great fear of mine, as I despise them. When Christmas turns into a filthy grayish-brownish thing that appears as though it was forgotten a century back and soaked continuously from then on, you are aware that it receives the name of a green Christmas! Request no explanation from me as to why. To quote Lord Dundreary, ‘there are thome thingth no fellow can underthtand.’”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0052 }

“Nell, have you ever boarded a street car only to find out that you had no money on you to pay the fare? I experienced that recently. It feels terrible. Upon boarding the car, I possessed a nickel. I believed it was located in my coat's left pocket. After I was settled comfortably, I searched for it. It was absent. A cold chill ran through me. I searched inside the opposite pocket. Still absent. A second chill hit me. Subsequently, I searched inside a small interior pocket. It was entirely useless. I suffered two chills at the same time.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0053 }

“Removing my gloves, I placed them upon the seat, and I searched through every one of my pockets once more. There was no sign of it. I got to my feet, shook my clothing, and subsequently inspected the floor. A crowd of individuals returning home from the opera packed the car, and every person gazed at me, though I no longer concerned myself with a minor matter of that nature.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0054 }

“However, my fare was nowhere to be found. My conclusion was that I had likely placed it inside my mouth and accidentally gulped it down.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0055 }

“Uncertainty overwhelmed me. I pondered whether the conductor would bring the streetcar to a halt and force me off in disgrace and humiliation. Could I perhaps persuade him that my situation stemmed purely from my own forgetfulness, rather than an attempt by a dishonest person to steal a ride under fraudulent claims? I longed desperately for the presence of Hector or Orlando. They were absent, however, precisely because I desired them to be there. Had I possessed no wish for them, they would have appeared in great numbers. Meanwhile, I remained unable to choose what I ought to tell the conductor upon his approach. The moment I formulated a single explanatory statement in my thoughts, I doubted anyone would accept it, forcing me to draft a different one. Relying on Providence appeared to be the sole option left, though it offered me no more reassurance than it gave the elderly woman who, upon being instructed by the captain amid a tempest to place her faith in God, cried out, ‘Oh, Captain, is it as bad as that?’”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0056 }

“Precisely at the expected instant, after all expectation was gone, and while the ticket collector was presenting his container to the rider beside me, the location where I had placed that miserable piece of money abruptly came back to my mind. It had not been consumed by me in the end. Quietly, I extracted it from my glove's forefinger and thrust it inside the container. I beamed at all the people and experienced a sense that the world was lovely.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0057 }

Going to Echo Cottage proved to be just as delightful as numerous other enjoyable vacation excursions. Nell and Isolde returned there via the familiar path through the beech woods, taking along a lunch basket. Echo Cottage, having remained shut continuously from the time of Miss Rosalind’s wedding, was temporarily opened wide to the breeze and light of the sun again, and the glow of firelight shone once more within the tiny rooms. The fragrance from Miss Rosalind’s rose bowl continued to saturate the atmosphere. One could scarcely credit that Miss Rosalind would not enter briskly in a moment, her brown eyes sparkling with welcome, and that Belinda the Fourth, wearing a blue bow and a broad smile, would not appear suddenly at the doorway. Cedric, as well, appeared to linger nearby, accompanied by his magical imaginations.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0058 }

“It truly causes me to feel somewhat like a phantom returning to see the moon’s ancient glimpses,” Nell chuckled. “Let us step outside to discover whether the echoes remain present. Fetch the aged horn. You can still find it stationed in back of the door to the kitchen.”
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0059 }

Across the pale stream, the echoes remained in their usual place, just as bright as silver and as abundant as they had always been; and once they no longer replied, the girls secured Echo Cottage once more and departed during the flawless thirty minutes that come after the pink and yellow hues of a winter sunset.
{: #nw-v03-c07-p0060 }
